findings.statement: The calibrated Lloyd–Taylor response reproduces established thermal behavior; near-ties do not demonstrate a new ecological law.
findings.applicability: Forward complete dates within calibrated contexts; related site/treatment labels are not independent geographic replications.
findings.limitations: Frozen thermal coefficient stayed near 200 K because optimizer scaling was limited. Preserve that version and its qualification; 96 context amplitudes are real calibration costs.
falsification: Keep all same-date context records together and fit context amplitudes only on earlier dates.
Preserve finite negative/high flux and explicitly report sites lost through missing 5 cmtemperature.
Compare directional wetting with drying, absolute change and reoptimized no-pulse controls; cluster sensitivity by related site labels.
findings.prior_art: Lloyd–Taylor and rewetting effects are established prior art; this is a small calibrated-context refinement. This review uses retained prior-art records only; it performs no new literature priority adjudication.

equation_or_program.expression: Rhat_c=A_c exp[E0(1/(10+46.02)-1/(T+46.02))], E0=200.000005K in original frozen state.
